subject.title: Gateway becomes slow or times out under multi-session / multi-agent load

question: Is the current v2026.6.11/current-main mitigation set enough to close #92057, or should maintainers keep it open until the reported Weixin/Codex multi-agent workload is replayed or split into narrower issues?
rationale: Automation cannot safely infer that partial handler fixes resolved the broad availability report because the issue has credible live evidence, current release contains only slice mitigations, and the remaining work may require choosing a transcript/session-maintenance policy.

options.title: Keep Broad Tracker And Require Live Proof
options.body: Leave #92057 open, gather sanitized current-release latency evidence for the reported workload, and only close or split after the remaining slow handler is identified.

options.title: Split Remaining Bottlenecks
options.body: Create or promote narrower canonical issues for raw transcript caps, compact latency, history/log reads, and channel-lane stalls while leaving #92057 as the parent until the split is complete.

options.title: Close After Maintainer-Accepted Proof
options.body: Close only if maintainers accept fresh v2026.6.11/current-main proof showing the large-store workload no longer causes Gateway RPC timeouts or message delivery stalls.

recommendation.title: Keep Broad Tracker And Require Live Proof
recommendation.body: Leave #92057 open, gather sanitized current-release latency evidence for the reported workload, and only close or split after the remaining slow handler is identified.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent release and gateway/session cleanup history makes this the best available owner for deciding the proof bar and tracker scope.
